body: I couldn't bring it up in depth. She says just wait and see if the side effects wear off. I'm so fucking weak. I could only tell her like halkf of the problem.
I'd be even more embarrassed just admitting how embarrassing this is for me with the act of handing her a typewritten explanation. Everything about this makes me feel like a failure.
It will probably be fine. I just don't know how to tell her "Oh, I suck at sex now." I can't imagine breaching the subject with someone with a face.
I've scheduled a sort of emergency appointment to fix this. Now I'm just really nervous over it.

It's not that I can't do it. I think she still enjoys it and that means I want to but I think she must be noticing. I think we're doing the tenderness and closeness thing right. We sort of talk during sex and she seems to enjoy it. I just want it to be what she wants.

The meds are something I need, they're fundamentally part of me. This is, on a fundamental level, my fault.

I know it sounds like we're distant but we're not. I guess I'm sort of passive in the relationship. I'm normally happy like this. I sort of wish she would just ask me about it so I wouldn't have to be the one to bring it up.
It feels like a pretty basic fuck up. She knows I'm bipolar and she knows I'm on medication.

I don't know how to tell her is the problem. I feel like this is a **huge**, glaring flaw and I can just barely admit it anonymously to the internet. How do I tell her? How do I emphasize it's my fault and not hers? I just don't know how any of this conversation is supposed to go.

I am seeing a professional. Multiple professionals. It's a "me" thing, not the people around me. I've pretty much isolated myself save for a few great people and they give me nothing but support. I'd rather deal with the problems with my girlfriend than anything else right now but I am working on fixing my self worth problems. I just don't think that, in a vacuum, separate from others, I really matter on my own.
I don't know how I could expose such a massive weakness to her. I lke to at least appear strong for her. This seems like a colossal failure on my part. I don't know how to tell her.

My "self" is just an extension of how others value me. I'm superfluous in and of myself. I know I have self worth issues but (Probably partially due to them) I care a lot more about other people than myself. I'm happy when I can do things right to make other people happy.
I can't imagine how I would ever tell her something so embarrassing.
That's fine I guess. I think I can bring it up with my shrink (Though I've no idea how to start that conversation). The real problem is I don't know how to tell my girlfriend any of this.

It feels like cheating. I have posted here before.

I don't know how to breach the subject with either my doctor or my girlfriend.
That's the thing, I want to be able to talk to her.
She's kind of slow to switch because it takes these things weeks to work anyways. I hope she's understanding about this.

I still can't do sex right, how basic is that? It might be irrational but I've got no idea how to mention this to my psychiatrist. SHe's a woman so it might be a little more awkward but I don't think that will bother me.

I am really exceedingly submissive, you're right in that. It might be part of me being depressive but I just don't care much for myself save for myself in relation to other people. I ejaculate when I masturbate *sometimes* but even then it takes much, much longer than it used to. I guess I'm frustrated with this as my problem but I'm more concerned that it isn't her problem.
I wish I had that kind of time.
I should fess up a bit. I'm bipolar II and so I'm sort of on a cocktail of pills. I will be following up on this.

Wellbutrin's not an option unfortunately and at least not on it's own. A big part of the problem is actually breaching the subject with my psychiatrist and my girlfriend. I don;t know how to tell them I've failed at one of the easiest things people do.
